# Ideation Hub platform

This folder is the single description of the Ideation Hub schema, the REST API, and the Model Context Protocol tools. The developer and requirements plugins point here. Do not copy these files into another plugin.

Load only the file you need:

- `references/schema.md` — record types, durable identifiers, revisions, status words, and trace links
- `references/mcp.md` — Model Context Protocol tools, permissions, and the suggest-versus-edit rule
- `references/rest-api.md` — REST routes and lifecycle behavior

Credential setup for a person is in the platform plugin `README.md`, one directory above this skill when the plugin is installed as a whole. The secret is never written in these files.

When this skill folder is copied next to `ideation-hub-developer` and `ideation-hub-requirements-agent` in one skills directory, those plugins look for `../ideation-hub-platform/references/`. When the three plugins are installed as sibling directories, they look for `../../../ideation-hub-platform/references/`, which is the same directory through the `references` link at the platform plugin root.

# MCP tools

Canonical catalog of the Ideation Hub MCP server. Tool arguments, permissions, and the suggest-versus-edit rule live here. The requirements plugin says when to author a record. The developer plugin says when to design, implement, or assess. Neither plugin repeats this catalog.

## Endpoint and auth

Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC at `POST https://api.ideationhub.me/api/mcp` (also `/api/v0/mcp` and `/mcp`). No SSE. `GET` returns server metadata.

Preferred headers: `X-IH-Client-Id: ${IH_CLIENT_ID}` and `X-IH-Client-Secret: ${IH_CLIENT_SECRET}`. The plugin `mcp.json` sends those headers. A bearer token from `POST /api/oauth/token` also works. Token request and errors: `rest-api.md`.

`initialize` returns protocol `2025-03-26` (or `2024-11-05` when requested), server `ideation-hub-mcp`. `tools/list` and `tools/call` require an agent credential. Omit `productId` to use the credential's current product. A product outside the grant is **403**. `ih_list_products` returns only granted products.

Never paste, echo, log, or print the client secret or an access token.

## Permissions

| Permission | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | Read and search. |
| Suggest (`propose`) | Writes land in the issuer's Review queue until a human Accepts. `suggest` and `propose` are the same permission. |
| Edit (`editDirectlyProductIds` or an `edit` scope) | A write without `mode: "suggest"` or `"propose"` changes the living record. Pass `mode: "suggest"` to queue a proposal anyway. |
| `delivery:write` | Append a development-phase event. Direct. Not a proposal. |
| `status:write` | Record a confirmation review or a status assessment. Direct. Never edits a title, a body, or a trace link. |

`review` is not a scope. Agents cannot Accept or Reject (**403**). Missing permission is **403**. Do not work around a 403 with another tool or credential.

**Write rule.** If the credential has direct edit on the target product and the call does not pass `mode: "suggest"` or `"propose"`, the change is applied to the living record and audited with the agent client id and the issuer user id, except that a direct edit while a proposal is pending is **409** `pending_proposal_exists`. Amend that proposal instead. Otherwise the call is a pending proposal (`proposalId`, `reservedHumanId`, `status: "pending"`, `reviewUrl`) on the issuer's Review queue. A trace link with exactly one pending-add end is stored with that requirement instead of a standalone proposal (`outcome: "bundled"`). Both ends existing: `outcome: "proposed"`. Direct edit: `outcome: "applied"`. Two pending adds stay one pending proposal and are hidden from standalone Review until both ends are approved. `mode: "edit"` without direct edit is **403**.

The developer plugin always passes `mode: "suggest"` on design and implementation writes unless the user, in that conversation, explicitly asks for a direct write. That is a plugin rule on top of this mechanism.

### Trace link review

- **One end is a pending add:** a Suggest link is stored with that requirement (`outcome: "bundled"`, `bundledWith` is its Human Readable Durable ID), either direction. No standalone Review item. It shows on that requirement's Review card. Accept keeps it and records `approvedLinks`. Reject or withdraw of the add hides it. A requirement with only a pending edit counts as existing.
- **Both ends exist:** the link is its own Review item (`outcome: "proposed"`, `proposalId`). Accept applies the add or the soft-remove. Reject and withdraw leave the trace unchanged.
- **Both ends are pending adds:** one pending proposal, not bundled and not shown in standalone Review while either end is pending. Accepting one end does not approve the other. Accepting the link early is **409** `ends_pending`. The trace is written when the last pending end is accepted.
- Direct edit writes the row (`outcome: "applied"`). Read-only is **403**. Removing a link: Suggest files a removal proposal; direct edit soft-removes it.

Soft delete is a proposal for Suggest, and applies immediately when that credential has direct edit.

## Tools

| Tool | Permission | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ih_list_products` | read | `{folderId?}`. Granted products (`directEdit` per product) and visible folders |
| `ih_get_chain` | read | `{productId?, includePending?, includeObsolete?, tag?, tags?}`. Profiles, requirements, and links. `includePending` keeps unapproved rows. `includeObsolete` defaults to true; pass false for living records. Optional `tag` or `tags` (AND, case-insensitive) |
| `ih_search` | read | `{query, types?, status?, includePending?, tag?, tags?, limit?, cursor?, productId?}`. Hybrid meaning and keyword search across requirements, profiles, PRD sections, verification specs, evidence, and pending proposals. Returns each match with its best passage, `score`, and `matchReason`. An exact human id ranks first |
| `ih_search_requirements` | read | `{query, types?, status?, productId?, limit?, tag?, tags?}`. Keyword listing by human id, title, and body. Not meaning-based. Tag filters are AND |
| `ih_get_requirement` | read | `{id, productId?}`. Human id (`PRD-001`) or UUID, revision, design fields, tags, inbound and outbound links, `pendingProposal` (null or the one pending add or edit, including `payload` and `canAmend`), `pendingProposalIds` |
| `ih_get_neighbors` | read | `{id, direction?: up\|down\|both, depth?, includePending?, includeObsolete?, productId?}`. `depth` defaults to 1. Pending neighbors are kept and obsolete ones dropped unless you pass otherwise |
| `ih_validate_against_trace` | read | `{id?, proposedPayload?, productId?}`. Duplicate title, missing profile or parent, orphan. Does not write |
| `ih_list_review_queue` | read | `{status?, source?: all\|agent\|human\|mine, type?, productId?, tag?, tags?}`. Each item's tags merge the payload and the target requirement |
| `ih_list_sections` | read | PRD sections in order, with summaries |
| `ih_propose_requirement` | suggest or edit | `{type, statement, title?, profileNameOrId?, parentId?, mockupUrl?, repoPath?, prUrl?, commitSha?, testPath?, lastResult?, tags?, mode?, productId?}`. Add BN/UN/PRD/SD/UXD/CD/IMPL/VT/VER/UT |
| `ih_propose_edit` | suggest or edit | `{id, title?, statement?, expectedRevision?, proposalId?, mockupUrl?, repoPath?, prUrl?, commitSha?, testPath?, lastResult?, tags?, addLinks?, removeLinks?, addProfileIds?, removeProfileIds?, mode?, productId?}`. Revise. Amends the one pending add or edit on that requirement in place (`amended: true`, same `proposalId`). `addLinks` and `removeLinks` are arrays of `{type, targetId \| targetProfileId}`. On a User Need, `addProfileIds` and `removeProfileIds` are shorthand. Link changes apply with the edit at Accept. A conflict then is **409** `link_conflict` or `duplicate_link`. **409** `pending_proposal_exists` or `ambiguous_proposal`: amend or pass that `proposalId`. `expectedRevision` mismatch is **409**. A no-op is **422** |
| `ih_propose_bulk_push` | suggest or edit | `{items, links?, dryRun?, mode?, productId?}`. `dryRun` does not persist or consume human ids. It checks types, required fields, duplicate titles, and that parents and link ends exist. It does not check link direction |
| `ih_propose_profile` | suggest or edit | `{action: add\|edit, id?, name, roleIntent, mode?, productId?}` |
| `ih_create_requirement` / `ih_update_requirement` | edit only | Direct aliases. Optional `tags`. Suggest-only is **403** |
| `ih_set_tags` | edit only | `{id, tags, productId?}`. Replaces tags. Does not create a revision. Suggest-only is **403** |
| `ih_link_requirements` | suggest or edit | `{sourceId, type: addresses\|realized_by\|checked_by\|refined_by, targetId?, targetProfileId?, productId?}`. Pass exactly one of `targetId` or `targetProfileId`. A User Need to User Profile link uses type `addresses` and `targetProfileId` only. Outcomes: `applied`, `bundled` (`bundledWith`), or `proposed` (`proposalId`). **422** `link_pair_not_allowed`, `profile_not_in_product`, or `link_target`. **409** `duplicate_link`. Proposing the same pending link again returns the existing proposal |
| `ih_unlink_requirements` | suggest or edit | `{linkId?, sourceId?, type?, targetId?, targetProfileId?, productId?}`. Soft-remove by `linkId` or source + type + target. To remove a User Need to User Profile link, pass `targetProfileId` instead of `targetId`. Reject or withdraw leaves the link |
| `ih_lifecycle_action` | suggest or edit | `{id, action, targetType?, reason?, mode?, productId?}`. Actions: `withdraw_proposal` (proposal id only), `withdraw_requirement`, `reopen_proposal` (withdrawn add-link at version 1), `reopen_requirement` (edit), `obsolete`, `delete_draft`, `reclassify` |
| `ih_restore_draft_title` | suggest | Title-only repair of the caller's pending add. Does not change the proposal |
| `ih_create_section` | suggest or edit | Add a PRD section |
| `ih_rename_section` | suggest or edit | Rename or nest a PRD section |
| `ih_delete_section` | suggest or edit | Delete a PRD section. Requirements in it become unassigned |
| `ih_reorder_sections` | suggest or edit | Reorder all PRD sections |
| `ih_set_section_summary` | suggest or edit | Set a PRD section summary |
| `ih_assign_sections` | suggest or edit | Place many PRDs into sections in one change |
| `ih_record_development_phase_event` | delivery:write | `{requirement, phase, sourceId?, requester?, evidenceUrl?, occurredAt?, productId?}`. Append one development-phase event. Direct, not a proposal. The developer plugin records `phase: "design_ready"` at handoff |
| `ih_get_revision_status` | read | `{id, productId?}`. Per revision: derived completeness and coverage, the latest assessment or null, and `differs`, `completenessDiffers`, `coverageDiffers`, `completenessComment`, `coverageComment`. REST: `GET /api/requirements/{id}/revision-status` |
| `ih_record_confirmation_review` | status:write | See below. Direct. Do not pass `mode` |
| `ih_record_status_assessment` | status:write | See below. Direct. Do not pass `mode` |
| `ih_subscribe_requirement_status` | read | `{id, revisionAccepted?, deploymentCompleted?, statusChanged?, productId?}`. Ask to be notified about one Product Requirement. Sending the same subscription again updates the flags. Notices stay in an inbox. There is no outbound webhook |
| `ih_list_requirement_notifications` | read | Inbox for this credential, newest first |

Section tools are listed with the purpose the product documents. If `tools/list` shows a more specific argument schema for a section tool, use that schema. Do not invent arguments.

How to retrieve a small slice versus a whole product is the requirements plugin's `references/retrieval.md`. How to judge implementation and test coverage is the developer plugin's `references/assessment.md`. Those files use the tools above. They do not redefine them.

## Confirmation review

`ih_record_confirmation_review`. REST: `POST /api/requirements/{id}/confirmation-reviews`.

| Argument | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Product Requirement human id or uuid |
| `revision` | Revision number |
| `recordKind` | `implementation`, `deployment_event`, or `test` |
| `recordId` | Implementation or test human id or uuid, or the deployment completed event uuid |
| `evidenceUrl` | Optional http(s) link |
| `productId` | Granted product, when you are naming one |

The same revision, record, and evidence returns the existing row. Pass `productId` when the credential can open more than one product.

## Status assessment

`ih_record_status_assessment`. REST: `POST /api/requirements/{id}/status-assessments`.

| Argument | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Product Requirement human id or uuid |
| `revision` | Revision number |
| `implementationCompleteness` | `unimplemented`, `partially_implemented`, or `fully_implemented` |
| `testCoverage` | `untested`, `partially_tested`, or `comprehensively_tested` |
| `completenessComment` | Optional |
| `coverageComment` | Optional |
| `evidenceUrl` | Optional http(s) link |
| `productId` | Granted product, when you are naming one |

An identical latest assessment for that revision returns the existing row. Say verdicts to a person in words. Pass the snake_case values to the tool. If the tool schema on the call lists different spellings, use the schema.

When to confirm, what counts as complete, and what counts as tested are PRD-180 in the developer plugin. This catalog only names the calls.

# REST API and lifecycle reference

This is the canonical REST reference for Ideation Hub. The developer and requirements plugins point here. Load this file when you call the REST API directly or need the exact behavior of a lifecycle action. The MCP catalog (`mcp.md`) covers the same operations. Every route below is also mapped under `/api/v0/...`.

## OAuth 2.0 `client_credentials` token

`POST /api/oauth/token` (also `/api/v0/...`; every route below is dual-mapped):

```json
{ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": "$IH_CLIENT_ID",
  "client_secret": "$IH_CLIENT_SECRET", "productId": "<uuid, optional>" }
```

- **200** `{ access_token, token_type: "Bearer", expires_in, productId }`. Omit `productId` for the credential's home Product; a sent one must be on its allow-list.
- **401** wrong secret / revoked. Re-mint when the token expires.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or call MCP with `X-IH-Client-Id` and `X-IH-Client-Secret` and skip the token. The token pins tenant + Product. MCP may pass `productId` only when that product is on the credential grant; otherwise **403**.
- Permissions: `read`, `suggest` (stored as `propose`), and direct edit via `editDirectlyProductIds` or an `edit` scope. Missing permission → **403**. `review` is not a scope.

## Read calls

| Need | Call |
| --- | --- |
| All requirements on the Product | `GET /api/requirements` |
| One requirement | `GET /api/requirements/{id}` (human id or UUID) |
| Neighbors up/down the trace | `GET /api/requirements/{id}/neighbors?direction=up\|down` |
| TraceLinks | `GET /api/trace-links` |
| Profiles | `GET /api/products/{productId}/profiles`, `GET /api/profiles/{id}` |
| Full Profile → UN → PRD chain | `GET /api/products/{productId}/chain` (or `GET /api/chain`) |

## Change calls

| Change | Call | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add BN/UN/PRD | `POST /api/requirements` | `type`: `business_need`\|`user_need`\|`product_requirement`; `title`, `statement`. UN needs `profileId` or a `profileName` matching exactly one canonical Profile. PRD needs `unId` of a canonical UN; Accept writes the `addresses` link. |
| Edit | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/revisions` | `{ title?, statement?, proposalId?, addLinks?, removeLinks?, addProfileIds?, removeProfileIds? }`. The one pending add or edit on that requirement is updated in place, whoever filed it. `addLinks` and `removeLinks` are arrays of `{type, targetId \| targetProfileId}`. On a User Need, `addProfileIds` and `removeProfileIds` are shorthand. They are stored on the one pending edit, shown in `pendingProposal.payload`, and applied in the same transaction at Accept. A conflict at Accept is **409** `link_conflict` or `duplicate_link` and leaves the requirement unchanged. A new proposal is filed only when none is pending. Filing a second is **409** `pending_proposal_exists`. Legacy duplicates are **409** `ambiguous_proposal` (pass `proposalId`). |
| Link | `POST /api/trace-links` | `{ sourceId, type, targetId? \| targetProfileId? }`. Pass exactly one target. A User Need traces to a User Profile with type `addresses` and `targetProfileId` set to the profile human id (for example `UP-004`); do not also pass `targetId`. Suggest, exactly one pending-add end: stored with that requirement (`outcome: "bundled"`, `bundledWith`). No standalone Review item. Suggest, both ends existing: `kind=link` proposal; Accept adds only the named profile and keeps the others. Direct edit writes the row. Two pending adds stay a standalone proposal. **422** `link_pair_not_allowed`, `profile_not_in_product`, or `link_target` (both or neither target given). **409** `duplicate_link`. Proposing the same pending link again returns the existing proposal. |
| Unlink | `POST /api/trace-links/remove` | Soft-remove a User Need to User Profile link with `sourceId`, type `addresses`, and `targetProfileId`. Same applied-versus-proposed split as Link. To remove a requirement-to-requirement link, use `POST /api/trace-links/{id}/remove`. |
| Obsolete | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/obsolete` | |
| Un-accept | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/unaccept` | `{ targetRevision?, reason? }`. Accepted requirements only (status `proposed`). Anything else is **4xx** and nothing is stored. Moves that requirement back to pending (`unapproved`) and keeps its Human Readable Durable ID — no renumbering. When `targetRevision` is an earlier `@n`, that revision's title and statement are copied onto a **new** revision. History is not rewritten. TraceLinks stay. |
| Reclassify | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/reclassify` | `{ newType, reason? }`. Accepted (`proposed` or `approved`) and pending (`unapproved`) only; otherwise **422**. Assigns the next human id for `newType` and keeps the old id as an alias. |
| Delete draft | `DELETE /api/requirements/{id}` | Only living status `proposed`; else **422**. This is the hard-delete path and stays refused for humans (`noHardDelete`). |
| Soft delete | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/delete` | `{ reason? }`. Sets `deleted_at`, `deleted_by`, and `deleted_reason`. The row, human id, and TraceLinks stay. The requirement leaves lists, Review, and trace views; the links stay stored and stay hidden. Human ids are not reused. Product owners, tenant admins, and `edit_directly` holders apply it immediately. An agent with only the propose scope files a `soft_delete` proposal; Accept applies it. **409** `already_deleted` when it is already deleted. |
| Restore | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/restore` | Clears the soft delete and brings the requirement and its TraceLinks back. Same direct callers as soft delete. Propose-scope agents do not file a restore proposal. **409** `not_deleted` when it is still live. |
| Withdraw one proposal | `POST /api/proposals/{id}/withdraw` | `{ reason? }`. `id` is the proposal id. Closes that pending proposal only. A requirement human id or uuid is **422** `requirement_id` and changes nothing. |
| Reopen one add-link proposal | `POST /api/proposals/{id}/reopen` | `{ reason? }`. `id` is a withdrawn `kind=link` add proposal at version `1`. Same id, payload, and version. No trace is written. A removal is **422** `link_removal`. Any other status or version is **409** `not_withdrawn_v1`. Direct edit, product owner, or tenant admin. Suggest scope is **403**. `reopen_requirement` does not do this. |
| Withdraw pending requirement | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/withdraw` | `{ reason? }`. Only `unapproved`. Soft-removes the requirement and closes every pending proposal on it. The row and human id stay. **409** otherwise. MCP action: `withdraw_requirement`. |
| Reopen withdrawn requirement | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/reopen` | `{ reason? }`. Only `withdrawn`. Sets the requirement back to `unapproved` and reopens its add proposal. Other proposals stay withdrawn. Direct edit, product owner, or tenant admin. Propose-scope agents get **403**. |
| Profile add / edit | `POST /api/products/{productId}/profiles` · `PATCH /api/profiles/{id}` | `{ name, roleIntent }`; never invent `roleIntent`. |

- Failed propose → **422** (unknown `type` → **400**); no proposal is stored. A pending UN or Profile is not a valid parent — wait for Accept, then propose the child.
- **Un-accept and the same rule as edit and obsolete.** A propose-scope agent files a Review proposal. A human editor with `X-Write-Mode: direct`, or an agent whose credential has edit-directly on this Product, applies it immediately. Either way the applied change writes an audit entry with the actor, the before state, the after state, and a timestamp. Requirements are never hard-deleted.
- Reclassify follows the same propose versus edit-directly rule as edit and obsolete. A propose-scope agent files a Review proposal. A human editor, or edit-directly mode (`X-Write-Mode: direct` with the edit_directly grant, or an agent credential that has edit_directly), applies it immediately. The write records an audit entry with the actor, the requirement before, the requirement after, and a timestamp. The row is never hard-deleted.
- The old human id still resolves (`GET /api/requirements/BN-038`). The UI shows `formerly BN-038`. TraceLinks stay on the same row. Links whose direction no longer matches the new type are reported as `directionInvalidLinks` and are not dropped.
- **No-op edits:** do not propose an edit whose title and statement match the current revision. It adds Review noise and changes nothing.
- Never re-propose to dodge a Reject; ask the human.
- **Withdraw one proposal.** `ih_lifecycle_action` with `action: "withdraw_proposal"` takes a **proposal id**. It closes that proposal and leaves the requirement and every other proposal alone. A requirement human id or uuid is **422** `requirement_id` and changes nothing. `action: "reopen_proposal"` is the inverse for one withdrawn add-link at version 1. Same proposal id and payload. It does not write a trace. A removal is rejected. The creating credential, the credential recorded on the withdraw audit, or an editor may call it. A second distinct withdraw actor is a conflict and is refused.
  - To withdraw the pending requirement and every pending proposal on it, the user must ask for that explicitly. Then use `action: "withdraw_requirement"` or `POST /api/requirements/{id}/withdraw`.
  - To undo that, an editor uses `action: "reopen_requirement"` or `POST /api/requirements/{id}/reopen`. The requirement returns to pending and its add proposal reopens. Edit proposals stay withdrawn. Propose-scope agents cannot reopen.
  - *Example (PRD-038, 2026-10-30):* an agent passed `id: "PRD-038"` to `withdraw_proposal` when that action still treated the id as a requirement. The whole pending requirement closed. That call is now rejected. Pass the proposal id to withdraw one proposal.

## Status, confirmation, and development-phase routes

These are direct writes or reads. They are not proposals. `status:write` never edits a title, a body, or a trace link. `delivery:write` records a development-phase event.

| Need | Call |
| --- | --- |
| Derived and assessed status for each revision | `GET /api/requirements/{id}/revision-status` |
| Confirm an earlier implementation, deployment event, or test still applies to this revision | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/confirmation-reviews` |
| Record an implementation-completeness and test-coverage assessment for one revision | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/status-assessments` |

The MCP arguments for those calls are in `mcp.md`. How to judge a Product Requirement (PRD-180) stays in the developer plugin's `references/assessment.md`. This file does not add judgment rules.

# Source: references/schema.md

# Ideation Hub schema

Canonical description of record types, identifiers, revisions, statuses, trace links, and the fields those records carry. The developer and requirements plugins point here. They do not keep a second copy.

**Product:** `https://www.ideationhub.me` · **API:** `https://api.ideationhub.me`

Ideation Hub is a requirements workspace built on **design controls**: a traceable chain from business intent to verified product behavior. Each record answers one question. Links show how records connect.

## Record types

- **Business Need** (`BN-NNN`) — a business objective. *Purpose:* why the business invests. *Good one:* one outcome the business wants, measurable where possible, free of solution detail. A Business Need is what the owning business must accomplish for itself (revenue, cost, compliance, strategy, or operations), not for the sake of a customer.
- **User Profile** — who the product serves. *Purpose:* anchor needs to a real role. *Good one:* a clear `name` plus a `roleIntent` saying what that role is trying to get done. It declares only the actual person (who they are, their role and context), never their needs. Those are User Needs. It is a role or type of person with a job to do, never one capability. The API identifies it by `UP-` id, UUID, or exact name.
- **User Need** (`UN-NNN`) — what a user must be able to do. *Purpose:* the user's view of value. *Good one:* a verb phrase, one objective, linked to every Profile it serves. It states WHAT the user wants to achieve, never HOW. It `addresses` the Business Needs it serves.
- **Product Requirement** (`PRD-NNN`) — WHAT the product must do. *Purpose:* a buildable, checkable commitment. It `addresses` the User Needs and Business Needs it satisfies. It does not link directly to a User Profile.
- **Design & Implementation** (`SD-NNN`, `UXD-NNN`, `CD-NNN`, `IMPL-NNN`) — System Design, UX Design (`mockupUrl`), Component Design, and Implementation (`repoPath`, `prUrl`, `commitSha`).
- **Verification & Validation Tests** (`VT-NNN`, `VER-NNN`, `UT-NNN`) — Validation Tests (check User Needs and Business Needs), Verification Tests (check Product Requirements, designs, and implementations), and Unit Tests (`testPath`, `lastResult`: `pass` | `fail` | `not_run`). `passed` and `failed` are accepted spellings of the last result.

How to write a good title or body is the requirements plugin's rubric, not this file.

## Identifiers and revisions

Every requirement has a **Human Readable Durable ID** (`BN-`, `UN-`, `PRD-`, `SD-`, `UXD-`, `CD-`, `IMPL-`, `VT-`, `VER-`, `UT-` + number, sequenced per type inside a Product) plus a UUID and a revision `@n`. Human Readable Durable IDs never get renumbered or reused. A former ID still resolves; the record shows its new ID. Profiles use `UP-` ids the same way.

A revision label such as `@3` pins a version. Cite the ID, and the revision when the exact wording matters. Requirements are never hard-deleted.

## Status

`status` tells you whether a record is accepted (`proposed` or `approved`), pending (`unapproved`), or withdrawn, obsolete, or superseded. Default reads show accepted, living records. Ask for pending or obsolete records only when the task is about them.

`proposed` and `approved` both mean **accepted and living**. Only `unapproved` means a pending add. `obsolete`, `superseded`, and `withdrawn` are retired.

## Trace links

There are four link types:

- `addresses` — the more specific record is the source: UN addresses BN; PRD addresses UN or BN; a User Need addresses a User Profile (`targetProfileId`, not `targetId`).
- `refined_by` — a record is refined by a more detailed one. The broader record is the source.
- `realized_by` — a requirement or design is realized by a downstream design or implementation. The broader record is the source.
- `checked_by` — shown as "Verified by". A need, requirement, design, or implementation is checked by another record, such as a test. The broader record is the source.

Walking **up** answers *why* this exists. Walking **down** answers *how* it is delivered and checked. Every trace is many-to-many, with zero or more on each side, and existing links are always preserved. A record with no upward trace is allowed. Flag it as a coverage gap. It is not by itself a defect.

### Stored direction

`addresses` runs from the more specific record to the broader one.

`realized_by`, `refined_by`, and `checked_by` run from the **broader** record to the more specific one. The broader record is the source of the stored link.

Specificity order: BN < UN < PRD = VT < SD = UXD = VER < CD < IMPL < UT. The target of `realized_by`, `refined_by`, and `checked_by` must be at least as specific as the source.

The server checks direction strictly only on some paths. Check direction before every link.

### Allowed pairs

Allowed upward relationships (the more specific record traces up to the broader one). A Business Objective is also called a Business Need.

- Product Requirement → Business Objective and User Need
- User Need → User Profile
- System Design → Product Requirement
- UX Design → Product Requirement
- Component Design → System Design
- Implementation → Component Design, UX Design, and System Design
- Verification Test → Product Requirement, UX Design, System Design, Component Design, and Implementation
- Validation Test → User Need and Business Objective
- Unit Test → Implementation and Component Design

**Hard rule:** a Product Requirement never links directly to a User Profile. It reaches a profile only through a User Need. A User Profile is never linked to a design. A design is never `checked_by` a Validation Test. Validation Tests check User Needs and Business Needs. Verification Tests and Unit Tests check designs. The developer plugin states which of those design test links it records.

Which of those design links a particular plugin creates is that plugin's procedure. This file is the allowed set.

### `parentId` on a new record

- A Product Requirement takes `parentId` or `unId`. Accept writes `addresses` to that User Need.
- `parentId` on an SD, UXD, or CD writes `parent realized_by` the new record. Use it for the first justifying link. Do not also send that same link in `links` (`duplicate_link`).

### Revision pins

Every link records `sourceRevision` and `targetRevision` (shown as `@n`). A link is **stale** when either record it connects now has a higher current revision than the pin. Staleness is how you find records reviewed against old text.

## Tags and design fields

Tags are a free-form list (`tags: string[]`). Each tag is 1–32 characters from letters, numbers, spaces, and `_-./`, at most 20, trimmed and de-duplicated without regard to case. Omit `tags` to leave them unchanged. `[]` clears them. Responses always include `tags` (an empty list when there are none). `ih_set_tags` and `PUT /api/requirements/{id}/tags` replace the list without a new revision. `tags` on an edit replaces the whole list.

Design fields on UXD / IMPL / VT / VER / UT: `mockupUrl`, `repoPath`, `prUrl`, `commitSha`, `testPath`, `lastResult` (`pass`, `fail`, `not_run`). A User Need takes `profileNameOrId`.
